Welcome to Alien Meows!

Our team specializes in creative work like game design, art, and writing. We enjoy integrating science of all categories in our work to achieve games that anyone of all ages can play and still learn through it!
summary:
Our video game protagonist, Arte, is going to space for the first time in her life, and it's her chance to prove her competence! In Turn Right at Artemis, all the details and tasks done by astronauts before, during, or after the space mission is simulated through different mini-games that allow a player with no background to enjoy the game and learn along the way. Besides the mini-games system, TRAA is focused on decision-making which opens doors to the player to have their own unique experiences and different endings in every mission they play, a great ending is Acquired through a good planning and accounting for unexpected scenarios, for example, supporting the soft skills of the player. 
Also, Make sure to explore as much as you can during missions, perhaps you can find a secret achievement or a new discovery, who knows?
details:
Overview of TRAA

Turn Right at Artemis is a video game with multiple endings based on the decisions and performance of the player throughout the mission starting from preparations on earth, arriving on the planet for the mission, to landing back on earth. All the technical details and tasks assigned to astronauts are simulated by mini-games that give the general idea of what's done (like water extraction from Mars' soil, batching the radiation shields, EVA suit checks before leaving the spacecraft, etc). Certain items that the player chooses to carry into space make these mini-games easier, some items improve Arte's mental health, some unlocks certain secret scenarios, but the player has to mind the weight of the cargo when storing items.

Our game ensures that every player has a unique experience and is curious to explore space and how a space mission works. However, the game isn't limited to a young audience and can be experienced by players of any age or background even with its cartoonish style, which we considered during our story-writing stage.

The game was developed with Godot Engine, with a focus on reusability and modularity, making it easier to expand and maintain after establishing its core systems. We used data-driven systems for items and NPCs, alongside reusable mechanics for dialogue, interactions, inventory, and mini-games. This allowed us to add new content and features without repeatedly writing the same code, making development more efficient and flexible.

Tools Used

Godot (coding), Krita (art), Itch io (hosting), Claude Code.
